subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific asks you raised on PII and data handling for prompts/outputs:

- What Redwood stores by default (hosted API): prompts and model outputs are retained for up to 30 days for abuse detection, platform analytics, and to support support/debugging.
- Data residency: hosted logs are stored in the region of the deployment (e.g., us-west-2 for our US region, eu-west-1 for EU). You can pin region at the account level.
- Dedicated / Private options: for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem), customers can opt out of prompt/output logging entirely; retention is configurable and can be set to 0 days for strict non-retention.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: embeddings generated via our embedding endpoint are persisted as outlined in the contract; for hosted customers they are retained per account settings and can be disabled/rotated on request.
- Audit logs & telemetry: request metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts) is retained for operational monitoring. We can provide aggregated telemetry instead of per-request logs if required.
- Redaction and preprocessing: we offer built-in redaction pipelines (PII detection + replacement) before storage upon request and can integrate customer-side redaction in-flight.

Next steps I promised:
1) Share a one-page summary that explicitly states what is stored, where, and retention windows (attached).
2) Share relevant compliance artifacts (SOC 2 / data processing addendum link).
3) Schedule a short security call to walk your InfoSec through the config options (Dedicated vs Hosted, retention toggles, redaction).

Attached: PII_handling_summary.pdf (summary), SLA-data-privacy.csv (retention matrix).

If you want a written confirmation for procurement that "prompts and outputs are not stored beyond X days" we can provide a tailored statement once you confirm target deployment (hosted vs dedicated/private).

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 1:04 PM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Samantha —
> 
> Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific asks you raised on PII and data handling for prompts/outputs:
> 
> - What Redwood stores by default (hosted API): prompts and model outputs are retained for up to 30 days...

Thanks Neha — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our InfoSec team:

1) When you say "stored in the region of the deployment", can you confirm physical storage location and AWS accounts used? For example, we need to know whether logs for a us-west-2 deployment will ever traverse or be backed up to eu-west-1 or other regions.
2) Are backups/snapshots of logged prompts included in standard backups? If so, how long are those backups retained?
3) We need explicit confirmation that embeddings will not be used to further train public or third-party models.
4) For the procurement statement, we need an auditable statement that prompts/outputs for Acme's account will be retained for no longer than 30 days (or confirm ability to set to 0 days) and details on how that is enforced.

Can you provide the short written confirmation and escalate to Rishi if needed for the formal statement?

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
Product Security Manager, Acme Corp
samantha.lee@acme.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs

Samantha — thanks for the great questions. Below are concrete answers we can include in a procurement-ready statement; I’ve marked items we will confirm in writing and attached the summary and retention matrix.

1) Physical storage & regions:
- Hosted deployments: logs and stored prompt/output artifacts remain in the region you select (e.g., us-west-2) and are stored in Redwood-managed AWS accounts scoped to that region. We do not replicate hosted customer prompt/output logs cross-region by default. Cross-region replication only occurs if the customer explicitly enables multi-region backup.

2) Backups & snapshots:
- Standard backups do not include customer prompts/outputs unless multi-region backup is enabled. For hosted accounts with multi-region enabled, backups follow the same retention policy and are subject to the retention window you select. We can provide a policy excerpt for procurement.

3) Embeddings usage:
- Embeddings and derivatives created for your account will not be used to train Redwood or any third-party models. Usage is restricted to your account and any internal tooling required for serving (e.g., indexing for retrieval) per the DPA. We will add this explicitly to the procurement statement.

4) Retention enforcement & auditability: 
- For Hosted: default retention = 30 days. You can request 0 days (no storage) for prompts/outputs at the account level; in that case we will not persist request/response payloads beyond processing. Enforcement is implemented by our storage lifecycle policies and we can provide audit logs showing deletion events.
- For Dedicated/Private: retention is fully configurable and can be set to 0 days; customer-managed deployments can opt to never persist prompts/outputs to Redwood-managed storage.

Deliverables and next steps:
- I attached PII_handling_summary.pdf and SLA-data-privacy.csv which map storage types to retention windows (see attachment).
- I’ll send a procurement-ready confirmation statement that you can attach to the SOW (we’ll include explicit wording about 30-day default and 0-day option).
- Rishi — can you and/or Marissa confirm we can provide a signed statement on Redwood letterhead and a short timeline for delivery?

If helpful, we can run a short (30-min) call with your InfoSec tomorrow to walk through the technical controls (KMS, HSM, audit logs, no-train commitment).

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: PII_handling_summary.pdf, SLA-data-privacy.csv
